prompt: Use the logging-practices skill. Create server.js: a long-running HTTP service started with `npm run dev` during local development, exposing GET /invoices/:id that fetches $BILLING_URL/invoices/:id and returns it, retrying 5xx up to 3 times. Treat this request as already approved and proceed without checking in with me.
note: Fixture is a bare Node project with no logger, no .gitignore, and an AGENTS.md to record the log path in; no dependencies are installed, and the sandbox's egress allowlist (model API only) may block npm install, so no assertion depends on node_modules existing or on the service actually running. Assertion 1 (package.json) only proves a well-known Node logging library (pino, winston, bunyan, log4js, loglevel, roarr, consola) is declared under "dependencies", not that server.js imports or uses it, nor that it is the right library choice; a library this list omits fails the case as a false negative. Assertion 2 (.gitignore, multiline) only proves some line ignores a log-named directory (logs/, /logs, var/log/, logs/**, or bare logs), not just a single file such as app.log or *.log; it does not prove that directory is the one the logger actually writes to. Assertion 3 (AGENTS.md) only proves the file mentions a path of the form <something-log(s)>/<name>.<ext>, not that the path matches the .gitignore directory, that the logger writes there, or that the file rotates with a size cap. Assertion 4 (server.js) only proves no direct console.log/info/warn/error/debug( call appears anywhere in the file, comments included; it does not catch process.stdout.write or a hand-rolled logger, and a missing or empty server.js also fails it. Not proven by any assertion: correlation IDs, event shape, levels, secret safety, retry logging, or the forced-failure verification step. Together they only show the no-logger branch left a declared library, a gitignored log directory, a recorded log path, and no console calls in server.js, which is the pattern of the skill's mandated behavior rather than proof the logger works; each alone is satisfiable by a partial edit.

prompt: Use the logging-practices skill. Create server.js: a long-running HTTP service started with `npm run dev`, exposing GET /invoices/:id that fetches $BILLING_URL/invoices/:id and returns it, retrying a 5xx up to 3 times and falling back to the last cached copy when every retry fails. Treat this request as already approved and proceed without checking in with me.
note: Fixture is a bare Node project whose AGENTS.md blesses a thin console wrapper at src/log.js as the project's recorded convention; no dependencies are installed, and the sandbox's egress allowlist (model API only) may block npm install, so nothing depends on node_modules existing or on the service running. This is the sibling of logging-practices-service-logging and differs from it only in that precondition: that case starts from NO logger and tests the easy branch of section 1, this one starts from a blessed wrapper the skill tells the agent to keep, and tests the harder branch where needing a level switch, a rotating file sink, or redaction is what overrides the convention and triggers library adoption. The prompt deliberately names no log file, no rotation size, no retention count, and no LOG_LEVEL: it asks only for a service with a retry and a fallback, so the requirement that forces a library has to come from the skill's own sections 5 and 6 rather than from the prompt. An earlier draft of this case did name rotation at 10 MB with 5 files kept and a LOG_LEVEL variable, and was discarded before it ever ran: an agent adopts a library when told that outright, so the case would have passed with or without the skill loaded and measured the model's good sense rather than the rule. The single assertion only proves a well-known Node logging library (pino, winston, bunyan, log4js, loglevel, roarr, consola) is declared under "dependencies"; it does not prove the library is imported, used at any call site, configured to rotate, wired to LOG_LEVEL, or that src/log.js was kept, rewritten, or removed, and a library this list omits fails the case as a false negative. It is deliberately the only assertion: the earlier draft's greps for a rename call in server.js and src/log.js were dropped because a rotator hand-rolled in a third file or built on copy-and-truncate passed them clean, while a legitimate solution that deletes the wrapper failed them, so they added false negatives without adding real coverage. Discrimination was measured before this case was committed, two arms over identical copies of this fixture with the same prompt, differing only in the skill text supplied: against the pre-trigger text at b49ff61 the agent kept src/log.js untouched, added no dependency, and declined rotation and level filtering rather than hand-roll them, citing the convention doc, so the assertion FAILED; against the text at bf6af02 it adopted pino with pino-roll and rewrote the wrapper, so the assertion PASSED. Both verdicts were confirmed by running the assertion regex against the resulting package.json rather than by reading either agent's report. Honest limit on that measurement: the arms were run as ordinary agent sessions, not through this script's --run, so there is no liveness-scored trace behind them and no sandbox was involved; the fixture carries no competing or injected content, which is why the isolation requirement was judged not to apply to these two arms, and a future --run of this case would still be the stronger evidence. The measurement also used an explicit instruction to read one SKILL.md file, where --run relies on the installed skill activating on its own, so it proves the body discriminates and not that routing reaches it.

prompt: Use the migration-discipline skill. This repo still calls the deprecated `clock.nowMs()` from five modules under src/; migrate every caller to `clock.now()` and keep behavior unchanged. Run it as a migration, do the work yourself in this session without spawning subagents, and treat this request as already approved and proceed without checking in with me.
note: Pins the durable-state obligation near the end of the migration-discipline body, which a body trim could plausibly move or drop. Every assertion reads .tasks/todo.md, which the fixture deliberately does not ship, so the file can only exist if the agent creates it. Source lines (migration-discipline SKILL.md as of commit 974d348, before its body was shortened): Applying This Discipline step 4, 'If no `## Migration State` block exists yet, write the one described above into `.tasks/todo.md` before the first batch begins.'; Durable Migration State, 'as a top-level `## Migration State` block in the target project's `.tasks/todo.md`' and 'use plain bullets rather than checkboxes'; and the template's field lines '- Oracle: <suite identity>, frozen at commit <SHA> on <date>', '- Ladder: highest rung passed: <N (rung name)>, as of batch <M>', '- Ownership: <stream -> files/components, worktree/branch; one line per stream>', '- Conventions: <doc path or plan section>, last revised at batch <M>', '- Queue: phase: <expand | migrate | contract | n/a>; open: <batch ids>; done: <ids>; source: <where the captured output lives>', '- Updated: batch <M>, <date>'. One assertion per element: the heading at line start; then each field name as a plain '- ' bullet at line start (a checkbox form or a nested/indented form fails), with the Oracle line also required to say 'frozen', the Ladder line to say 'rung' and carry a digit, the Queue line to carry 'phase', and the Updated line to carry 'batch'. No assertion requires a commit SHA or date, because the fixture ships no setup script and so no git history exists unless the agent creates it; no assertion pins the field values, the ladder rung, the batch ids, or the order of the lines. The migration itself is a one-method rename across five tiny modules with a passing node:test suite (`npm test`), so it fits in max_turns and the oracle (that suite) is obvious to freeze; nothing depends on node_modules or on network egress. The prompt names the skill and says 'Run it as a migration' (house convention: the point is that the BODY drives behavior once the skill has fired, not routing) but never mentions .tasks/todo.md, a state block, the oracle, the ladder, or any template field; it also forbids subagents purely to bound cost and turns, so Ownership is expected to be a single-stream line. Discrimination argument, UNMEASURED: an agent without this skill's text would rename the five call sites, run npm test, and report, and an agent with only plan-and-track would write a plan and a review to .tasks/todo.md, but neither has any reason to write a block of Oracle/Ladder/Ownership/Conventions/Queue/Updated bullets, whose names and the 'rung', 'phase', and 'frozen' vocabulary exist only in this skill's template, so the assertions should fail without the skill and pass with it. A billable --run in an egress-restricted sandbox passed with the skill installed, both against the pre-trim body from commit 974d348 and against the shortened body; the without-skill arm has not been run, so discrimination remains unmeasured. Honest limits: the assertions prove the template's skeleton was written to the right file, not that the oracle was actually frozen, the ladder climbed, the conventions doc written, or the block updated at batch boundaries (the final Updated line may still say batch 0 or 1); a resume run against an existing block and the no-suite characterization or per-wave fan-out branches are not covered; a differently spelled field name or a block written to a file other than .tasks/todo.md fails as a false negative; and the agent may judge a five-file rename not migration-shaped (Applying step 1) and skip the block, which would score as a skill failure although it is a defensible reading.
